source.title: Do Physics Foundation Models Learn Generalizable Physics? A Bias-Aware Benchmark Across Physical Regimes and Distribution Shifts
source.authors: Meng-Di Chu; Yang Liu; Ayan Biswas; Han-Wei Shen

record.file_problem: not stated; full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling and pretraining behavior in PDE forecasting models, a new physical-model setting relevant to V5, and reports non-monotonic scaling and negative transfer. It does not fit or evaluate power laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many PDE error and distribution-shift results, but those do not test the listed language-model scaling claims. Only the model-size and pretraining comparisons are recorded because they bear on whether scaling behavior carries to physics models.
record.test_reason: The study compares fine-tuned PDE forecasting error across pretrained S/M/L checkpoints and pretrained versus scratch models. It never states parameter counts, fits no power law, and fine-tunes on a fixed, small benchmark set (200 trajectories per in-distribution IC family). Data is therefore a likely bottleneck, so non-monotonic size effects cannot show whether a power-law form holds (V5). Pretraining gain at matched size is not a scaling measure. The results are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that physics foundation models are conditional rather than universal generalists. They find richer data, pretraining and scaling give selective, non-monotonic gains that do not remove regime biases or give consistent OOD robustness. They argue for better transferable physical representations rather than only more scale.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PDE forecasting relative L2 error and comparisons among pretrained/scratch or S/M/L variants; it does not fit language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling laws. The comparisons use limited model sizes and no compute-optimal allocation sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by architecture and PDE family; the reported scaling analysis is under Mix-balance at the 10-step horizon.

fits_no_version.finding: Among fine-tuned pretrained PDE foundation models, error does not fall monotonically from S to M to L. Only 45.0% of 40 architecture–PDE pairs improve monotonically, 25.0% of M/L cells are worse than S, and L is best in 23 of 40.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With fixed small fine-tuning data, larger pretrained physics foundation models do not reliably give lower forecasting error.

fits_no_version.finding: Matched-size pretraining (pretrained-M vs scratch-M) gives negative transfer in 37.5% of architecture–PDE pairs, with mean gain −2.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-physics pretraining does not reliably improve downstream PDE forecasting at matched size.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized OOD ShiftDamage on Dynamic- and Joint-OOD groups rises from 4.22× (S) to 6.28× (L), versus 3.24× for scratch (Section 4.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling pretrained physics models improves train-seen error more than shifted-regime error.

record.problems: The paper measures PDE relative L2 forecasting error rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy, reports only a few model sizes, and does not fit power laws. Reported model-size comparisons do not establish whether a power law fits over several orders of magnitude.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant model-size or matched-size pretraining results omitted. Other PDE error, rollout, and distribution-shift results were excluded because they do not bear on the listed versions.

untested.parts: Power-law form of loss vs parameters, data or compute for physics/PDE models; no parameter counts, no fits, no data or compute sweeps.
Not addressed: no language-model pretraining loss.
No shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
No relation of downstream performance to scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents or fitting-choice comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' with V5 labels is overturned. S/M/L parameter counts are never given, no power law is fitted, and fine-tuning uses a small fixed dataset (data likely the bottleneck). Pretraining-gain rows are not scaling measures. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only in the discussion.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute; no power-law fits.
No small-run fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token counts.
No controlled comparisons of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.

The paper evaluates PDE forecasting error across a few model sizes and pretraining states, not power-law fits or exponents. It does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer beyond its PDE-model setup.
No downstream task performance or its relation to pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or comparison of curve-fitting and setup choices.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PDE forecasting models, matched-size pretraining and S/M/L pretrained comparisons under Mix-balance
reader_labels.reason: The reported scaling outcomes are mixed and often non-monotonic, so the evidence does not support a generally stable scaling form in this tested setting; see r1–r2 and r7–r9.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Reported PDE/model comparisons with negative transfer or inverse scaling
reader_labels.reason: Some larger or pretrained variants have higher forecasting error than their stated reference, contrary to a consistent error-decrease-with-scale expectation; see r3, r5, r12–r14.
